data.gender_notes: Banitha is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Banitha is a Sanskrit female name derived from the word 'Bani', meaning 'daughter of', and 'Tha', the name of Lord Vishnu. In Hindu mythology, Banitha is believed to be the daughter of Lord Vishnu and is often associated with love, compassion, and devotion. The name Banitha carries the meaning “Daughter of Lord Vishnu” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Banitha usually hope their child will grow to embody daughter of lord vishnu and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Banitha belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Daughter of Lord Vishnu.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Banitha total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

historical_references.reference: Banitah was a celebrated courtesan and a great poetess in the 16th century in Vijayanagara Empire, India. She was one of the six 'Navaratnas' or nine gems of the royal court of Emperor Achyuta Deva Raya. Her poems were known for their vivid descriptions, deep emotions and a unique blend of Carnatic music and Sanskrit language.

historical_references.reference: Banitadevi was a queen of the Chandela Dynasty in the 11th century in Central India. She is known for her devotion towards Lord Vishnu and her role in the construction of temples. She is considered a symbol of power and piety in Hindu mythology.
